cases.name: t1/ambiguous-relocation
cases.why:
diff@9.0.0 applyPatch discards the (nonsensical) @@ line number, relocates by context, silently picks the second of two equally good matches and reports success: "x
DUP
y
CHANGED
z
". T1 makes this patch invalid.

cases.name: t1/adjacent-duplicate
cases.why: Adjacent duplicates make overlapping occurrences, which must count independently.

cases.name: t1/no-match
cases.why: Zero occurrences is a HALT, not a relocation to the nearest thing.

cases.name: c6/advisory-line-numbers
cases.why: A wildly wrong @@ number must not prevent a unique context match from applying.

cases.name: t3/descending-hunks
cases.why: diff@9.0.0 applyPatch turns these eight lines into fourteen — its cross-hunk offset bookkeeping duplicates six lines and reports success. Sequencing each hunk against the content the previous one produced gives one deterministic answer instead.
cases.content:
a
b
c
d
e
f
g
h

expect.content:
a
B
c
d
e
f
G
h

cases.name: t3/ambiguity-created-by-earlier-hunk
cases.why: T3 verbatim: a hunk that satisfies T1 against the pre-patch content but not against the content an earlier hunk in the same patch produced must HALT.

cases.name: t2/insertion-into-empty
cases.why: The carve-out is oldPat.length === 0, and @@ -0,0 normalises to insertion index 0.

cases.name: t2/insertion-amid-duplicates
cases.why: A pure insertion has no pattern, so T1 does not apply even though the surrounding content is entirely duplicate lines. The @@ number is the only positional information there is.

cases.name: t2/insertion-index-after-an-earlier-hunk-shifted-lines
cases.why: Shrunk from the zero-context property, seed 2082756637. The second hunk is a pure insertion whose "@@ -3" numbers the pre-patch file, but the first hunk has already removed a line. Applying the header number literally against the current content inserts one position too late and yields "+++ b/content\n\na". T2 and T3 disagree here and the spec does not reconcile them; the header number is carried forward by the net line shift. See SPEC-FEEDBACK F6.
cases.payload:
--- a/content
+++ b/content
@@ -1,1 +0,0 @@
-a
@@ -2,0 +2,1 @@
+a
\ No newline at end of file

cases.name: c5/drop-trailing-newline
cases.why: The new side ends the file without a newline, so the terminator must be consumed.
cases.payload:
--- a/content
+++ b/content
@@ -2,1 +2,1 @@
-b
+c
\ No newline at end of file

cases.name: c5/gain-trailing-newline
cases.why: The old side is marked no-newline and the new side is not, so the result gains a terminator. Without this the round trip silently loses the final newline — the class of bug PB-1 exists to prevent.
cases.payload:
--- a/content
+++ b/content
@@ -2,1 +2,1 @@
-b
\ No newline at end of file
+c

cases.name: c5/marker-contradicts-match
cases.why: The old side claims to end the file, but the content it matches is newline-terminated. That is a genuine failure to apply, not something to paper over by normalising.
cases.payload:
--- a/content
+++ b/content
@@ -2,1 +2,1 @@
-b
\ No newline at end of file
+c

cases.name: c5/localised-marker
cases.why: GNU diff and git localise the marker text. §5.2 admits "\" as a hunk-line prefix without constraining what follows, so the prefix is what is matched, not the English string.
cases.payload:
--- a/content
+++ b/content
@@ -2,1 +2,1 @@
-b
\ Kein Zeilenumbruch am Dateiende
+c

cases.name: pb1/crlf-not-normalised
cases.why: A CRLF payload against LF content must fail to match rather than be repaired. The bytes are signature-protected and PB-1 forbids normalising either side.

cases.name: grammar/empty-context-line
cases.why: A blank context line loses its leading space to editor and mail pipelines, so a bare "" line is common in the wild. git, patch(1) and jsdiff all accept it; §5.2's hunk-line production does not. See SPEC-FEEDBACK F7.

cases.name: grammar/content-line-looks-like-a-header
cases.why: Content whose own lines read "--- a/content" must survive. Inside a hunk every line carries a prefix, so the payload is unambiguous — but a matcher that scans for headers line-wise instead of parsing will corrupt it.

cases.name: malformed/truncated-hunk
cases.why: diff@9.0.0 throws here. Normalised into the same rejection signal as every other failure.

cases.name: malformed/headerless-garbage
cases.why: diff@9.0.0 returns [{hunks: []}] for this and does not throw. Trusting the hunk count alone would make it indistinguishable from the N2 header-only no-op, silently turning malformed input into "applied cleanly, no change".

cases.name: noop/header-only
cases.why: The shape jsdiff createPatch emits when a === b. MUST NOT be rejected as malformed.

cases.name: malformed/empty-fenced-block
cases.why: An empty ```diff block yields an empty payload, which used to short-circuit to the N2 header-only no-op and validate with zero issues. It is neither no-op shape: E7/N1 cover the absence of a block, N2 covers a block carrying a header, and this has a block with no header. §5.2 makes header-block mandatory, so C1 applies and application is malformed. Found by review on PR #1.

cases.name: chain/root-only
cases.why: With no patches the canonical bytes are the root content and there is no tip.

cases.name: chain/applies-in-chain-order-not-array-order
cases.why: Order comes from NIP-10 e reply threading, never from the order the events arrived in.

cases.name: chain/prose-only-noop-is-a-valid-link
cases.why: A prose-only patch changes nothing yet still extends the chain, so p2 replies to it.

cases.name: chain/foreign-patch-never-enters-the-chain
cases.why: A foreign patch is an overlay; canonical bytes are unchanged by its presence (RC-2). The chain carries no patches, so the root is the tip (RC-5) and an overlay anchored there is clean, not stale.

cases.name: chain/root-author-reply-to-a-foreign-patch-is-ignored
cases.why: Such a patch is not a chain extension; adoption semantics are §11 future work.

cases.name: chain/self-fork-freezes-at-the-shared-parent
cases.why: Two root-author patches reply to p1, so bytes freeze at p1 and no tip is defined.

cases.name: chain/self-fork-resolved-by-deleting-one-branch
cases.why: Deleting one branch head leaves exactly one branch and the chain resolves onto it.

cases.name: chain/earliest-of-several-forks-is-the-freeze-point
cases.why: Two forks exist; the freeze point is the earlier one at the root, not the later one.

cases.name: chain/deletion-cascades-to-descendants
cases.why: Deleting p1 removes p2 with it, leaving an empty chain at the root state.

cases.name: chain/deletion-by-another-pubkey-is-ignored
cases.why: NIP-09 honours a kind 5 only from the target event’s own author.

cases.name: chain/kind-5-targeting-a-kind-5-has-no-effect
cases.why: NIP-09 defines no reversal, so p1 stays deleted.

cases.name: chain/deletion-observed-before-its-target-applies-retroactively
cases.why: Confluence: the same event set yields the same state whichever order it arrived in.

cases.name: chain/deleted-overlay-leaves-default-rendering
cases.why: Canonical bytes were never affected by the overlay, so only its rendering changes.

cases.name: chain/halt-freezes-at-the-last-applied-patch
cases.why: p3 is individually well-formed and still is not applied, because H1 admits no exception.

cases.name: chain/halt-is-not-sticky
cases.why: H1 is reevaluated on topology change: deleting the offending patch resumes the chain.

cases.name: chain/halt-upstream-of-a-fork-sets-the-bytes-and-the-fork-is-still-surfaced
cases.why: Both freeze conditions are live. The HALT is earlier in chain order so it determines the bytes, and SF-3 still requires the fork be surfaced though it did not determine content.

cases.name: chain/ceiling-aborts-application-and-is-never-a-halt
cases.why: A ceiling stops application before a verdict: neither resolved nor halted.

cases.name: chain/ceiling-leaves-an-overlay-unclassified
cases.why: A ceiling is not a conflict — the overlay may well apply — and the target is well defined.

cases.name: chain/overlay-clean-stale-and-conflict
cases.why: Each overlay is evaluated against its own target snapshot: clean at the tip, stale at an earlier position where the hunks still apply, conflict where they do not.

cases.name: chain/overlay-orphaned-downstream-of-a-halt
cases.why: The target has no defined resolved content, so no clean/conflict/stale verdict exists.

cases.name: chain/overlay-orphaned-on-a-fork-sibling
cases.why: A fork sibling has no canonical position, so an overlay anchored to it is orphaned.

cases.name: chain/overlay-degrades-to-beta-when-the-target-is-unobserved
cases.why: An unobtainable target degrades to β, and the overlay is never re-anchored elsewhere.

cases.name: chain/classification-does-not-read-trust
cases.why: Trust is a presentation-time filter over these results, so authorship cannot change them.

cases.name: chain/patch-whose-root-is-unobserved-is-retained
cases.why: Without the root pubkey the patch cannot be classified at all, so it is held, not dropped.

cases.name: chain/no-chain-over-a-binding
cases.why: A Binding is corrected by kind 5 plus a replacement, never by a patch.

cases.name: chain/metadata-root-resolves-like-a-product
cases.why: The canonical chain is defined over Product and Metadata roots alike.
